Full-year marketing teardown: Toon Blast

For all of 2025 Toon Blast ran no social ads at all. It grew anyway. In February 2026 it restarted, and by October it had 186 live ad placements. That switch is the whole story: the game did the work, then marketing was turned back on to press the advantage.

Content strategy

What the ads say

One line, one challenge: "Can You Blast All the Cubes?" No offer, no price, no season. The creative is the level itself, cut as a skill test.

318 of 320 placements, one script

What the creators say

Gameplay clips with a hashtag stack, no captions worth reading. The one that broke out is a 56.9M-view video from a general entertainment account, not a games channel.

Verdict

Worked. Toon Blast grew net bookings about 25% in FY2026, a fiscal year that ran April 2025 to March 2026. US paid social was dark for ten of those twelve months and returned only in February 2026. The growth came first; advertising came after it and then scaled hard through the rest of 2026.

What worked

  • One creative bet, repeated: a single challenge line across 318 placements.
  • Creator reach did the heavy lifting for free in 2025.
  • No discounting, no seasonal noise, no web funnel to maintain.

What didn't

  • Owned social is invisible: 93k views on 93 posts.
  • No search presence at all, brand term undefended.
  • Growth depended on one creator account for 96% of views.

Plays to copy

One line, one test

Pick the single hardest thing the product does and ask the viewer if they can do it. Ship one script, not twenty.

Watch: installs per creative

Buy the audience, not the channel

A 900k entertainment account delivered 57M views. Game accounts would have delivered a fraction.

Watch: views per dollar

Point ads at the store

No landing page, no funnel, one hop to the listing. Less to build, less to break.

Watch: store conversion

Spend after the signal, not before

Growth led in 2025; the ad restart came in 2026 once the game was working.

Watch: bookings vs spend

Method. SEEN means a call result or image showed it; INFERRED is reasoned from what was seen. Full-year scope replaces the skill's holiday window: January 2025 through November 2026, monthly. Counts are floors where the source caps out: the Meta pull stopped at 30 pages with more available.

Pulled 2026-11-22. Meta Ad Library US, SpyFu US, DataForSEO US, App Store US, Take-Two Interactive filings and earnings coverage. Creator spend is inferred from follower tiers because no post carries a paid label.

Built for a general account of the year, not a shopping window. Toon Blast is a Zynga title; Zynga is owned by Take-Two Interactive.
